group_assessment.group: Aldaz laboratory, Department of Carcinogenesis, University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, Science Park-Research Division, Smithville TX, with Mark T Bedford (same department) supplying the WW-domain methodology and Andrzej K Bednarek (Medical University of Lodz) as co-author. Six authors, Aldaz last and corresponding.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_gene: YES, and it is the originating laboratory: this group cloned WWOX and named FRA16D (Bednarek 2000, PMID 10786676, resolved this session), and its own references 3 and 4 are its prior WWOX papers. Measured on PubMed 2026-09-13: `Aldaz CM[Author]` 138 records, `Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX` 38. At the time of THIS paper the count was 5 (`Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX AND 1900:2004[dp]`), so in 2004 this was a young gene programme in the hands of the people who had just cloned it.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_disease: NO, and the separation is sharp and measurable. `Aldaz CM[Author] AND (epilepsy OR ataxia OR encephalopathy)` returns 8 records across a 138-paper career, and NONE of them is this one: in 2004 this laboratory's frame is cancer - FRA16D, LOH in breast/ovarian/oesophageal/prostate/hepatocellular tumours, xenograft suppression. The germline neurological phenotype did not exist in the literature yet (WWOX AND epilepsy/encephalopathy = 119 records today, the first of them years later).
group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 Observation and interpretation weigh differently here and the direction is favourable for the observation. The BIOCHEMISTRY is method-expert work: Bedford is a WW-domain specialist (`Bedford MT[Author] AND "WW domain"` = 19 records) and the four-ligand far-Western with eight WW domains and a GST-only lane is the standard assay of that field, run with its own positive controls (FBP11/PPLP, FBP21+FBP30/PPR, PIN1/PLT*P, YAP/PPPY each light up their own ligand). So the ligand-class result is strong observation from people equipped to make it. The INTERPRETATION is framed entirely by cancer biology and by a tumour-suppressor hypothesis, and every functional inference in the Discussion runs toward p53, JNK1, TNFalpha and NF-kB in tumour cells. Nothing in the group's 2004 competence bears on neurons, and the paper makes no neural claim - so the danger is not that this group over-read the nervous system, it is that a LATER reader could carry an in-vitro cancer-cell result into a neurodevelopmental claim. That is a risk about us, not about them.

field_density.reading: 🔴 The PPxY intersection is a literature of SEVENTEEN. 487 of 708 WWOX records mention the WW domain, but only 17 name the PPXY ligand and only 3 and 1 name SIMPLE and LITAF - so the motif that the whole WW1-scaffold logic rests on has been examined by name in about 2% of the gene's literature, and this 2004 paper is its primary. That is the context for treating it as load-bearing rather than historical: a near-empty intersection in a rare-disease mechanism is a signal, not an absence.

multihop.highest_value_debt: 7644498 (Chen & Sudol 1995) is the paper that DEFINED the Group I WW domain and supplied the WBP-1 PPPY peptide used as the ligand in Figure 1b. The entire 'PPxY = Group I' framing this repository inherits descends from it, and it has never been read here. 11042109 (Jolliffe 2000) is its mirror on the partner side: SIMPLE's PPSY is a NEDD4 ligand, so the motif WWOX binds is shared with an E3 ubiquitin ligase - a competition this paper names and does not test.

entries.proposition: THE LIGAND RESULT, AND IT IS A DIRECT BINDING EXPERIMENT RATHER THAN AN INFERENCE FROM A SCREEN: the N-terminal WW domain alone, and the tandem construct, bound the PPPY peptide. This is the primary evidence for the PPxY specificity that this repository's WW1-scaffold logic descends from.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE PANEL SUPPORTS THE PPPY RESULT AND QUALIFIES THE PAPER'S OWN ABSOLUTE NEGATIVE. On the WBP1 (PPPY) row, bands appear in the YAP, WWOX-1 and WWOX-1&2 lanes, with WWOX-2 and GST blank - so WW1 binds PPPY and the tandem does too, cleanly. The text's 'did not interact with any of the ligands tested' is therefore stronger than the panel: WWOX-2 shows faint phospho-threonine-proline signal. Each control behaves: FBP11 lights PPLP, FBP21 and FBP30 light PPR, PIN1 lights PLT*P, YAP lights PPPY.

entries.proposition: THE PPxY-DEPENDENCE SERIES, LANE BY LANE - AND ONE READOUT WEAKNESS THE TEXT DOES NOT NAME. For SIMPLE the series is clean and in the claimed direction: wild type binds, first-motif mutant is much weaker, second-motif mutant is unaffected, double mutant is absent - and the double mutant's total-protein lane is visibly the HEAVIEST of the eight, so the loss is not a loading artefact. For WBP-1, however, the pulled-down band sits at the SAME height as the asterisked nonspecific GST band that runs across all eight lanes, so 'mutagenesis demonstrated it is the target' rests on intensity at a position the paper itself marks as nonspecific.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3a top panel, GST-WWOX1&2 pulldown, eight lanes: 1 N.C., 2-4 WBP-1 WT/mPY1/mPY2, 5-8 SIMPLE WT/mPY1/mPY2/mPY1&2. A band marked with an asterisk runs across every lane at one height. Lanes 2 and 3 are strongly darkened at that height and lane 4 is faint. A distinct LOWER band appears only in the SIMPLE series: strong in lane 5, clearly fainter in lane 6, strong in lane 7, absent in lane 8. Bottom panel, total protein: lanes 2-4 comparable, lanes 5-7 comparable, lane 8 markedly heavier than every other lane.

entries.proposition: WW1 IS BOTH SUFFICIENT AND REQUIRED FOR ENDOGENOUS SIMPLE, ON THE PANEL: the tandem construct and WW1 alone both pull SIMPLE down, WW2 alone pulls nothing, the WW1-inactivating mutant loses the band and the WW2-inactivating mutant keeps it. An unexplained upper band is present in all three right-panel lanes including the mutant that lost binding, so the SIMPLE identification within that panel rests on the lower band alone.

Left panel lanes 1-4: GST alone blank, WWOX-1&2 a strong band, WWOX-1 a strong band, WWOX-2 blank. Right panel lanes 5-7: WWOX-1&2 shows an upper band plus a strong lower band, mut1 shows the upper band with the lower band absent, mut2 shows the upper band plus a fainter lower band.

entries.proposition: LOCALISATION IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PARTNERSHIP AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH IT, and the paper's own strongest localisation claim is the NEGATIVE one against mitochondria. Endogenous WWOX overlaps the Golgi 58K marker substantially, shows essentially no overlap with MitoTracker, and overlaps SIMPLE only PARTIALLY, with each protein also occupying areas the other does not.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 4, nine panels in three rows of three, MCF-7 cells with DAPI-blue nuclei in the merges. Row a-c: anti-WWOX green perinuclear, anti-Golgi 58K red in the same perinuclear arc, merge showing yellow overlap. Row d-f: anti-WWOX green perinuclear, MitoTracker red in a distinct broader cytoplasmic pattern, merge showing green and red side by side with little yellow. Row g-i: anti-WWOX green and anti-SIMPLE red, merge showing partial yellow overlap with separate green-only and red-only territories.

verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: 🔴 WAIVED FOR 16 OF 24 ENTRIES, WITH THE ARGUMENT PER ENTRY IN EACH ENTRY'S OWN `abstract_anchoring_waived` FIELD. Eight entries DO carry a companion `abstract_snippet`, because the abstract genuinely states the PPXY identification, the N-terminal domain, the five array candidates, SIMPLE's PPSY requirement and the MCF-7 co-localisation. The other sixteen cannot be anchored there for two structural reasons that no rewording fixes. FIRST, SEVEN ARE PIXEL FACTS: faint bands in two lanes of a far-Western row, uncircled dark spots on an autoradiograph, a lane count of four where the text says five, band-by-band intensities against an asterisked nonspecific band, residue substitutions read off a schematic, and the presence or absence of a band in individual mutant lanes. An abstract is prose and cannot attest a panel; this repository's own rule is that a caption is not its figure, and an abstract is further away still. SECOND, NINE ARE METHOD OR QUALIFICATION SENTENCES THAT THE ABSTRACT OMITS OR CONTRADICTS BY SIMPLIFICATION: the GST construct residue boundaries (AA 16-53, AA 53-94), the nine-residue biotinylated peptide sequence, the 27,648-clone array scale, the fact that one of the five clones was never identified, Table 1's PPAY/PPSY/PPPY family, the authors' own hedge that both constructs showed reduced binding, the named conflict with the mitochondrial-localisation literature, and the Discussion's statement that p53's proline-rich region contains no PPXY motif. The abstract says 'the specific proline-rich ligand for WWOX as PPXY' and 'five candidate-binding partners' WITHOUT qualification - so quoting it beside these entries would import the very overstatements they exist to record. Anchoring them to the abstract would be worse than waiving: it would make a simplification look like corroboration.
